Plot Andre Punt's mean age at length for conditional age-at-length data

Source: R/plot_composition_diagnostics.R
plot_composition_andre.Rd

For conditional age-at-length data, plot the observed and expected mean age in each length bin, and the standard error of the mean age, for each year. These are "Andre's plots" from r4ss::SSplotComps() (subplot 12).

plot_composition_andre(
  dat,
  interval = 0.9,
  flip = FALSE,
  fleet = NULL,
  ncol = NULL
)

Arguments

dat

A tibble returned from convert_output() that contains conditional age-at-length data (see bigskate_caal), or conditional data in any other format accepted by prepare_composition_data() with conditional = TRUE.

interval

Number. Coverage of the intervals around the observed values. Default: 0.90, corresponding to 90% intervals

flip

Logical. TRUE/FALSE; put age (the mean age or its standard error) on the horizontal axis and length on the vertical axis, as in a growth curve. The default (FALSE) puts length on the horizontal axis, as in r4ss.

fleet

Character or numeric vector. Fleet(s) to keep, matching either the fleet name (e.g., "Fishery_current") or the fleet name with its partition (e.g., "Fishery_current (retained)"). NULL keeps all fleets. Default: NULL

ncol

Number. Number of facet columns. NULL lets ggplot2 choose. Default: NULL

Value

A ggplot2 object with one row of panels per year (and per sex and fleet when there is more than one): mean age at length on the left and standard error of the mean age on the right.

Details

Within each year and length bin, the observed and expected mean ages are \(\sum_a a\, o_a\) and \(\sum_a a\, e_a\), and the standard errors are the corresponding standard deviations of age divided by \(\sqrt{N}\), where \(N\) is the number of fish aged in the length bin. Following r4ss, the interval for the mean is the observed mean plus or minus the normal quantile times the observed standard error, and the interval for the standard error is based on the chi-square distribution. Observed values outside the intervals, or expected values that consistently differ from the observed values, suggest mis-specified growth or variability in length at age.

The statistics are calculated separately for each sex. Unlike r4ss, which combines sexes, this avoids jumps in the expected values when the ratio of sample sizes varies between sexes. Length bins with no observations or no sample size are omitted. Plot one fleet at a time with fleet, and subset years by filtering dat.

Equivalent plots in other packages

r4ss: r4ss::SSplotComps() subplot 12 (Andre's plots of mean age and standard deviation for conditional age-at-length data).

See also

prepare_composition_data(), plot_composition_bubble()

Examples

plot_composition_andre(
  dplyr::filter(bigskate_caal, year %in% 2016:2018),
  fleet = "WCGBTS"
)


# Age on the horizontal axis
plot_composition_andre(
  dplyr::filter(bigskate_caal, year %in% 2016:2018),
  fleet = "WCGBTS",
  flip = TRUE
)
